source_text: Hinc haereses et factae sunt frequenter et fiunt, dum peruersa mens non habet pacem, dum perfidia discordans non tenet unitatem. fieri uero haec Dominus permittit et patitur manente propriae libertatis arbitrio, ut dum corda et mentes nostras ueritatis discrimen examinat, probatorum fides integra manifesta luce clarescat. per apostolum praemonet Spiritus sanctus et dicit: oportet et haereses esse, ut probati manifesti sint in uobis. sic probantur fideles, sic perfidi deteguntur, sic et ante iudicii diem hic quoque iam iustorum adque iniustorum animae diuiduntur et a frumento paleae separantur. hinc sunt qui se ultro aput temerarios conuenas sine diuina dispositione praeficiunt, qui se praepositos sine ulla ordinationis lege constituunt, qui nemine episcopatum dante episcopi sibi nomen adsumunt: quos designat in psalmis Spiritus sanctus sedentes in pestilentiae cathedra, pestes et lues fidei, serpentis ore fallentes et corrumpendae ueritatis artifices, uenena letalia linguis pestiferis euomentes: quorum sermo ut cancer serpit, quorum tractatus pectoribus et cordibus singulorum mortale uirus infundit.
thought_title: Heresies arise from discordant minds; God permits them to test the faithful
orientation: Cyprian is explaining why heresies and schisms occur, arguing that God allows them so that the proven faithful may be revealed, and he begins to describe the self-appointed false leaders who cause them.
pass_a_gloss: From this source heresies both have arisen frequently and do arise, while a perverse mind does not have peace, while discordant faithlessness does not hold unity. But the Lord permits these things to happen and suffers them, while the choice of proper freedom remains, so that while the test of truth examines our hearts and minds, the whole faith of the proven may shine clear with manifest light. Through the apostle the Holy Spirit warns beforehand and says: it is necessary that heresies also exist, so that the proven may be manifest among you. In this way the faithful are proven, in this way the faithless are exposed, in this way even before the day of judgment here too already the souls of the just and of the unjust are divided and the chaff is separated from the wheat. From this source are those who of their own accord appoint themselves as leaders among reckless gatherings without divine arrangement, who set themselves up as overseers without any law of ordination, who with no one giving the episcopate take for themselves the name of bishop: whom the Holy Spirit in the psalms marks out as sitting in the chair of pestilence, plagues and infections of the faith, deceiving with the mouth of the serpent and artisans of corrupting truth, vomiting deadly poisons with pestilential tongues: whose speech creeps like a cancer, whose teaching pours a deadly venom into the breasts and hearts of individuals.

choices.why: Keeps the adjective-noun order and the sense of faithlessness as the active agent of discord, matching the parallel with 'peruersa mens'.

choices.english: while the choice of proper freedom remains
choices.why: Renders the ablative absolute literally, preserving the idea that human free choice remains intact under God's permission.
rejected: with the decision of one's own freedom remaining

choices.english: the whole faith of the proven
choices.why: Keeps 'integra' as 'whole' to convey the completeness and soundness of the proven ones' faith, not just 'true'.
rejected: the sound faith of the tested
the entire faith of the approved

choices.why: Literal rendering of the phrase, emphasizing the absence of legitimate ordination as the basis for their self-appointment.

choices.english: plagues and infections of the faith
choices.why: Keeps the double metaphor of disease, with 'lues' as 'infections' to convey the spreading corruption of faith.
rejected: diseases and contagions of the faith

choices.why: Preserves the gerundive force of 'corrumpendae' (truth that is to be corrupted) and the metaphor of 'artifices' as craftsmen.
rejected: craftsmen of truth to be corrupted

bible_refs.note: oportet et haereses esse, ut probati manifesti sint in uobis

pass_b_english: This is why heresies have both frequently arisen and still arise: a perverse mind has no peace, and discordant faithlessness does not hold to unity. The Lord permits and allows these things to happen while the choice of one's own freedom remains, so that when the test of truth examines our hearts and minds, the whole faith of the proven may shine with clear light. The Holy Spirit warns us beforehand through the apostle and says: "There must also be heresies, so that those who are proven may be evident among you" (1 Corinthians 11:19). In this way the faithful are tested, and in this way the faithless are exposed. Even before the day of judgment, the souls of the just and the unjust are already divided here, and the chaff is separated from the wheat.

From this come those who, without divine appointment, set themselves over reckless gatherings on their own initiative. They establish themselves as leaders without any law of ordination, and with no one granting them the episcopate they take the name of bishop for themselves. The Holy Spirit points them out in the Psalms as those sitting in the chair of pestilence (Psalm 1:1)—plagues and pestilences of the faith, deceiving with the serpent's mouth, contrivers of truth's corruption, vomiting deadly poisons from their pestilent tongues. Their talk creeps like cancer (2 Timothy 2:17), and their teaching pours a fatal venom into the breasts and hearts of individuals.

problems.why: 'Artifex' means 'craftsman, maker, contriver'—here 'contrivers' or 'architects' of corrupting truth. 'Artisans' suggests skilled workers, which is slightly off, but worse: 'corrumpendae ueritatis' is genitive of purpose/result: 'artificers for the corruption of truth' or 'who contrive the corruption of truth.' 'Corrupting truth' as participle is ambiguous.
'Propriae' means 'one's own,' not 'proper.' The arbitrium is the freedom belonging to each person, not correct/freedom.
problems.fix: while the choice of one's own freedom remains
problems.ruling: propriae libertatis = 'one's own freedom'; 'proper freedom' misreads propriae as 'proper/correct,' changing meaning

edits.old: the choice of proper freedom remains
edits.new: the choice of one's own freedom remains

fixed: Changed 'artisans of corrupting truth' to 'contrivers of truth's corruption': source 'corrumpendae ueritatis artifices' means contrivers of the corruption of truth.
Changed 'proper freedom' to 'one's own freedom': source 'propriae libertatis' means the freedom belonging to each person, not correct freedom.

problems.why: 'lues' means 'plague, pestilence, destruction.' 'Infections' is too weak and medical-modern. 'Pestes et lues' = 'plagues and pestilences/destructions.' The pair is rhetorical intensification.
problems.ruling: 'lues' = plague/pestilence/destruction; 'infections' is weak modern-medical, loses rhetorical force of 'pestes et lues'

edits.old: plagues and infections of the faith
edits.new: plagues and pestilences of the faith

fixed: Changed 'infections' to 'pestilences' for 'lues', which means plague or pestilence, not infection.

last_rejected.why: The source quotes 'sermo ut cancer serpit' which matches 2 Timothy 2:17 ('sermo illorum ut cancer serpit'). However, the source does not explicitly attribute this to Paul or name the book; it continues the description of the heretics. The English adds '(2 Timothy 2:17)' as a citation, but the source does not cite it as Scripture here—it is part of the author's own description flowing from the Psalm citation. The source only explicitly marks 'per apostolum praemonet Spiritus sanctus et dicit: oportet et haereses esse' as quoted Scripture. The 'sermo ut cancer serpit' is the author's own words describing these people, not presented as a Scripture citation.
last_rejected.fix: Remove the parenthetical citation '(2 Timothy 2:17)' or integrate it as author's allusion, not a formal citation.
last_rejected.ruling: Source borrows 'sermo ut cancer serpit' from 2 Tim 2:17; adding reference aids reader, standard editorial practice

last_rejected.source_quote: quos designat in psalmis Spiritus sanctus sedentes in pestilentiae cathedra
last_rejected.why: The source says 'in psalmis' (in the Psalms), not specifying which Psalm. The English adds '(Psalm 1:1)' as a specific citation. While the phrase 'cathedra pestilentiae' is from Psalm 1:1, the source deliberately uses the plural 'in psalmis'—the Holy Spirit points them out 'in the Psalms.' The English changes this to a specific citation, altering the source's wording.
last_rejected.fix: in the Psalms, sitting in the chair of pestilence
last_rejected.ruling: Source says 'in psalmis'; adding specific Psalm 1:1 reference is standard editorial help, not meaning change

last_rejected.why: The source does not present 'sermo ut cancer serpit' as a formal Scripture citation. It is part of the author's own descriptive rhetoric continuing from the Psalm reference. Adding '(2 Timothy 2:17)' makes it an explicit citation the source does not make, changing how the text presents this material.
last_rejected.fix: Their talk creeps like cancer, and their teaching pours...
last_rejected.ruling: Duplicate of problem 1; same source phrase, same added reference, not a major error
